Reviewed both proof steps and exact evaluation-space, law and pi-lambda suppliers. Every subset of the extended count range is Borel, including infinity. Finite coordinate cylinders form a generating pi-system containing the whole configuration space; equality of two probability measures on it extends by the elementary equality lambda-system and Dynkin theorem. Empty S and zero configurations are included. No disjointness reduction or AC is needed. Last–Penrose Proposition 2.10 (ii)⇒(i), full concluding argument at printed p. 15 / PDF p. 27 (zero-based page 26), supplies this exact cylinder method. The reader mistakenly labeled the printed page 16, while retaining the correct PDF page.

Reviewed all four steps and exact mixed-binomial, product uniqueness/Tonelli, kernel and scalar-law suppliers. Add-one evaluations are measurable; the left evaluation kernel has the common compact exhaustion already proved (all configuration masses finite on K_n), satisfying the integration theorem. Identical product factors permit coordinate permutation by rectangle uniqueness. Nonnegative sums and iterated integrals justify reindexing n p_n=lambda p_(n-1), with no cancellation and infinity allowed. The zero mass branch gives both sides zero; n=0 contributes an empty sum. Repeated locations are counted per occurrence. No AC is used. Source statement is Theorem 4.1, but the finite forward proof is Theorem 4.4 with m=1 at printed pp. 30–31 / PDF pp. 42–43; its full finite argument was read. The original carrier archive matches pre hash 18486a13a508c9fbbc37d93a705468d945045eb22232d70ea33f433948c8b3b2; reader-post has only locator and terminal-newline differences. Corrected the claimed proof location and synchronized manifest.

Independently reviewed all seven steps and exact compact-exhaustion, finite-law, scalar-law, product, weighted-sum, MCT and compact-closed suppliers. Disjoint Borel cells have finite mass and later cells miss K_m. Coordinate support events form a measurable probability-one E; zeroing off E makes every realized configuration locally finite. Finitely listed coordinates make their union countable without selecting enumerations. Step 3.2 displays finite Poisson convolution and joint independence; decreasing lower rectangles in 4.1 give product count laws. Step 5.1 handles infinite intensity by the exponential-series tail bound. Empty S, zero cells, atoms and finite/infinite total mass are covered. Countable Choice and DC enter only the countable-product theorem in 2.1. Reader:48:1 is confirmed nonfatal: the old finite_checks entry cited 3.1 for a calculation in 3.2. Replaced the inaccurate risk review with this accurate complete review.

Reviewed all 14 steps and each of the 28 declared supplier interfaces. Campbell follows from the mean-measure lemma, with infinite counts included. Laplace discards zero coefficients, handles infinite positive-coefficient intensities, and uses MCT on 1-exp(-eta(s_n)), avoiding a signed or decreasing MCT error. Configuration addition is measurable and remains locally finite; the evaluation kernel has the common compact exhaustion. Restriction/background laws are independent by finite disjoint-atom count cylinders and two pi-lambda extensions; finite Mecke plus Tonelli sums over disjoint cells without any new existence or choice assumption. Deletion is applied only on the measurable occurrence domain, removes one occurrence and retains multiplicity. Conversely, add-one tests give finite means and the joint count recurrence; zero means and p_0 normalization yield independent Poisson masses, and compact exhaustion treats infinite-intensity counts. Cox formulas average only the supplied conditional Poisson kernel; the nonnegative second-moment identity includes infinity. Its two finiteness conditions imply finite first moments by t<=1+t², legitimizing the variance subtraction. Empty S, f=0, extended-infinite f, atoms and deterministic/zero directing measures are consistent. No extra AC or directing-law uniqueness is asserted. Corrected step 1.3 to counting measure: h has configuration-space domain, so applying it to an arbitrary locally finite measure was ill-typed. Accepted the reader Laplace source correction after reading Theorem 3.9, PDF pp. 35–36.
